authority: Mark, FR14 pass 64: live-A/B serving on a Tier-B credential; promoted-default only after exact16 QC parity

bounds.name: determinism_bitwise
bounds.statement: Every determinism case must be bitwise identical across all repeats within a process, AND the per-case output/LSE digests must be identical across independent processes.

bounds.name: output_ulp_concentration
bounds.statement: At least 90% of characterized output elements must agree with the incumbent within 2 ULP.

bounds.name: output_max_abs_delta
bounds.statement: The largest output disagreement with the incumbent must be at most 4 bf16 steps at the scale of the tensor's own maximum. Expressed scale-free as max_abs_delta <= 4 * 2^-8 * reference_max_abs, evaluated per case and taken at its worst.

bounds.name: lse_max_ulp
bounds.statement: The fp32 log-sum-exp must agree with the incumbent within 8 ULP everywhere. LSE feeds the acceptance/rejection arithmetic, so it is held tighter than the bf16 output in relative terms.

bounds.name: lse_max_abs_delta
bounds.statement: Absolute LSE agreement, as a second check that does not depend on the ULP grid.

bounds.name: argmax_flips_vs_exact_no_worse_than_incumbent
bounds.statement: Against a float64 dense reference on the SAME probe cases, the candidate must disagree with the exact argmax no more often than the incumbent does. This is the bound that makes the arm-versus-arm flip rate interpretable: a disagreement between two approximations is not a defect unless the candidate is the worse approximation.

bounds.name: output_rms_vs_exact_ratio
bounds.statement: Candidate output RMS error against the float64 reference, divided by the incumbent's on the same case, at its worst. Catches a systematic bias that a ULP histogram would not: a kernel can be uniformly slightly wrong and still sit within 2 ULP everywhere.

bounds.name: lse_rms_vs_exact_ratio
bounds.statement: The same test on the log-sum-exp.

bounds.name: nonfinite_agreement
bounds.statement: No element may be finite in one arm and non-finite in the other, in output or LSE. A NaN or Inf that appears only under split-K is a defect, not a rounding difference, at any magnitude.

does_not_grant: promoted-default status (Mark: only after exact16 QC parity)

acceptance of a Tier-B credential for an arm not explicitly marked tier-b

Author: claude-picktest <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   Wed Aug 19 21:47:39 2026 +0000

    sites 17 and 16: one workload truth in the patcher, and a mint that can actually fail
    
    SITE 17. exact16 attempt 3 ran 4m16s to engine init and died at the first
    served token: _fr13_fa2_qrow32_b1_require_exact4 read only the legacy EXACT4_*
    spelling and compared against the hardcoded canonical four, so no caller value
    could satisfy it -- sixteen ids are not four, and unset is not four either. The
    workload-table landing converted the RECORD accessor and never this GATE, 600
    lines away in the same file.
    
    The fix is not to teach the gate the table. It is to stop the gate knowing what
    a workload IS: require_declared_workload(tier) asks
    _fr13_fa2_qrow32_b1_tier_b_workload(), the same accessor the record uses. Both
    spellings, both-must-agree, unknown refuses -- all inherited rather than
    restated, because a second statement of the same rule is exactly what site 17
    was. Tier A stays ruled to exact4 and refuses anything else, so widening the
    tier-B route does not widen the byte-gated one.
    
    CENSUS of legacy readers, both roots: the patcher's require_exact4 (converted)
    and its production RECORD fields task_ids/subset_sha256, which were literals --
    the same defect one field over, and the comment directly below them already
    warned about it ("an emitter that states an identity instead of reading it will
    eventually describe a run that did not happen"). It was right: a record of an
    exact16 serve would have named the four exact4 tasks. Both converted. The
    launcher production gate keeps its exact4 pins, adjudicated: tier A is ruled to
    the canonical four. Everything else is pass-through.
    
    SITE 16 (a). The promoted default minted PATCH_SOURCE_SHA256 by hashing
    scripts/fr13_patch_fa2_tree_bias.py -- the same file the selector gate then
    compares against disk. A value derived from an artifact cannot test that
    artifact: the gate was x == x, unfailable however stale the credential was. It
    is now minted from the credential's SEALED identity (grep, so the host keeps no
    Python dependency before docker), making the gate sealed-vs-disk.
    
    SITE 16 (c) CENSUS, two instances. The second,
    FR13_FA2_QROW32_B1_TIER_B_CREDENTIAL_SHA256, is RECORDED NOT REPAIRED: on the
    caller path the check is real, on the default path it is x == x and cannot be
    otherwise, because a file's own digest has no external source short of a fourth
    literal pin needing re-pinning at every re-seal. What guards that path is the
    credential's internal binding and verify-tier-b in the container. The exception
    set is asserted exactly, with its reason beside it.
    
    SITE 16 (b), AND IT IS RED ON PURPOSE.
    test_the_staged_credential_is_sealed_against_this_patcher asserts the real
    pair. This landing moved the patcher digest bec74652 -> 188c95aa while the
    staged credential is sealed at bec74652, so it fails until the runner
    re-seals. That is the one-edit-one-reseal window made visible on CPU instead
    of discovered on GPU.
    
    A DETECTOR THAT NARROWED UNDER REFORMATTING, recorded because it nearly went
    unnoticed: site 16's mint became a MULTI-LINE ${VAR:-$( ... )}, and site 15's
    import-precedes-owner projection -- a single-line regex -- silently stopped
    matching the very name it was written for. Caught only because a mutation test
    asserted a count of 2 and got 1. A projection that narrows when the code is
    reformatted is worse than none, because nothing announces the loss. Both
    spellings match now.
    
    Also: the F1 mutation proofs were literal find/replace strings and broke on
    every edit to the block they guard; they are positional now, anchored on the
    INDENTED in-block line -- stripping first matched the top-level VAR=${VAR:-}
    normalisation 470 lines earlier and deleted everything between, a mutation that
    "worked" while testing nothing.
    
    Mutation proofs: exact16 declared + sixteen ids reaches and passes the serve
    gate; exact4 unchanged; random1024_calibration passes with empty pins
    (measurement 1 rides this); legacy-only caller unchanged; mismatched pins
    refuse; tier A refuses exact16. Full sweep: one new failure, the intended
    re-seal signal.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

hunks.class: GATE — decides which serves are REFUSED; returns identity data. No kernel selection, no arithmetic.

precondition.why_the_banked_probe_evidence_REMAINS_VA: the nine bounds measure the KERNEL's numerics -- determinism, ULP concentration, LSE and output deltas against a float64 reference. A gate decides whether the kernel runs, not what it computes. Since no line of this diff touches a tensor operation, the selector sentinel or num_splits, the banked probe measurements describe this binary exactly as before. Saying so explicitly rather than inheriting the provenance-only claim.
